title: GCellComplex — cellular G-action compatibility
body_html:
GCellComplex

A Prop class asserting that a MulAction G X on the face poset $X$ is cellular — i.e. compatible with both the face relation and the dimension function.

Signature

lean class GCellComplex (G : Type*) [Group G] (X : Type*) [PartialOrder X] [AbstractCellComplex X] [MulAction G X] : Prop where smul_le : ∀ (g : G) {E F : X}, E ≤ F → (g • E) ≤ (g • F) smul_dim : ∀ (g : G) (E : X), AbstractCellComplex.dim (g • E) = AbstractCellComplex.dim E

  • smul_le: the action preserves the face relation $E \preceq F \Rightarrow g \cdot E \preceq g \cdot F$.
  • smul_dim: the action preserves dimension $\dim(g \cdot E) = \dim E$.

Combined, these two axioms say $G$ permutes the cells while preserving the face-and-dimension structure — the abstract analogue of "$G$ acts by cellular homeomorphisms."

Design choice: layered typeclasses, no bundling

The cell complex (AbstractCellComplex — dimension function on a face poset) and the MulAction are not bundled into GCellComplex; both are separate typeclass inputs. GCellComplex G X is purely the compatibility requirement on top. This lets a downstream file speak of "an abstract cell complex" without mentioning $G$, and later add "...on which $G$ acts cellularly" as a separate assumption.

Fix helper

Under the same module, the fixator of a cell is exposed as

lean def Fix {G : Type*} [Group G] {X : Type*} [MulAction G X] (E : X) (g : G) : Prop := g • E = E

— a plain predicate on $G$, no cell-complex structure needed. This is the workhorse for the QFD / induction axioms P1, P2 (see Quasi-fundamental domain and [[node:equivariant_sheaves.induction_GxP_X]]).
